title: Shared Parameters Governance (GUID-First, Citizen vs Visitor)

applies_to: All TIVERIT Revit projects using shared parameters
Project setup and ongoing parameter management

definitions.definition: A parameter whose identity is defined by a GUID and intended for reuse across contexts.
The authoritative identity of a shared parameter. Names are labels only.
Registered, governed shared parameter approved for cross-project use and distributed via official releases.
Shared parameter observed in project reality but not registered or approved for cross-project governance.
Authoritative, versioned record of citizen parameters, GUID-first and independent of projects.
Generated implementation artifact derived from the registry, such as a Revit shared parameter TXT release.
Periodic observational capture of parameters present in a project model.
Comparison output between a Project Snapshot and the Registry showing differences, collisions, and risks.

requirements.statement: Shared parameter identity is GUID-first: if the GUID does not match, it is not the same parameter, even if the name matches.
The Shared Parameter Registry is the authoritative source for shared parameter identity and semantics.
Revit shared parameter TXT files shall not be treated as sources of truth; they are derived implementation artifacts.
Citizen parameter meaning and identity may only be changed through registry versioning and governance approval.
Any parameter promoted to Citizen shall be issued through a registry-derived release.
Visitor or provisional parameters shall be clearly identified as project or provisional parameters.
Visitor or provisional parameters shall not impersonate Citizen parameter names or intentionally create name collisions.
Visitor or provisional parameters shall not silently propagate beyond project boundaries.
Promotion to Citizen status requires stabilized semantics, ownership assignment, registry entry, versioning, and governance approval.
Projects shall produce periodic Project Parameter Snapshots for governance monitoring.
A Delta Engine shall compare Project Parameter Snapshots against the Registry and classify differences.
Delta classification shall include unknown parameters, name collisions with differing GUIDs, deprecated parameters still in use, missing required Citizen parameters, and usage escalation signals.
Built-in Revit parameters shall not be stored in the Shared Parameter Registry.
Migration or repair actions shall preserve traceability and shall not silently rewrite parameter meaning.
Retired GUID identities shall not be reused without an explicit governance decision.
